description: GTEx (Genotype‑Tissue Expression) Database – Overview The GTEx project is a NIH Common Fund–funded, multi‑institution consortium (Broad Institute, Columbia University, NY Genome Center and others) that has assembled a public reference atlas of human gene regulation. It contains paired whole‑genome‑sequencing (WGS) and bulk RNA‑seq data from ≈ 900–1,000 post‑mortem donors, covering 54 non‑diseased tissue sites (including 11 brain regions, heart, lung, liver, whole blood and two transformed cell lines). In its final release (v8), GTEx provides ≈ 17,000 RNA‑seq samples and genotype data for each donor, together with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL), splicing QTL, allele‑specific expression, and a single‑nucleus RNA‑seq atlas of ≈ 209 k nuclei across eight tissues. Purpose & Use Cases GTEx was created to map how inherited genetic variation influences transcript abundance and splicing in a tissue‑specific manner, thereby furnishing a mechanistic bridge between genome‑wide association studies and molecular phenotypes. Researchers use GTEx to: - Prioritize causal variants from GWAS; - Investigate tissue‑specific regulatory mechanisms; - Model genotype‑by‑environment interactions; - Develop statistical methods for eQTL and transcriptomic analysis; - Benchmark new computational pipelines. Key Features & Unique Aspects - Largest multi‑tissue human genotype–expression resource; - Uniformly processed WGS, RNA‑seq, and QTL pipelines with detailed metadata (age, cause of death, ancestry). - Public portal (gtexportal.org) offering searchable gene‑level expression, eQTL browsers, single‑cell atlases, and API access. - Integrated biobank of residual tissues for downstream functional studies.
